Speaking at a meeting of the National Security and Defense Council on winter resilience, Zelensky accused Western allies of deliberately depriving Ukraine of missile supplies “aimed at making Ukraine, so to speak, more willing to compromise” in peace talks with Russia.

After meeting with NATO's Rutte, Zelensky said“ "It is important to reduce all red tape and make the necessary political decisions. Literally every day, the lives of people here in Ukraine depend on the determination of our partners in Europe and the United States.”

Russia launched 24 ballistic missiles in a night attack on Wednesday, killing at least 17 people. Preliminary data from the Ukrainian air force showed that its defenses shot down 98 of the 115 drones fired by Russia overnight, but none of the ballistic missiles.

On Wednesday, Zelensky said that in the first half of 2026, deliveries of air defense missiles from Ukraine's allies had fallen to a third of their 2025 level.

Ukraine has lacked American-made Patriot interceptors capable of shooting down Russian ballistic missiles since the beginning of the war. But in recent weeks, an acute shortage has manifested itself, with Moscow beating Kiev, on average, every three days in July alone. 

Zelensky said that the shortage of interceptor missiles was mainly “caused by Macron's secret talks with Trump to let the war continue over and over again, so that France can rearm during this time.”

The Patriot missile systems are the only system in Ukrainian service capable of intercepting the Russian Iskander-M, S-400 and Zircon missiles, according to the Ukrainian air Force.

Russia often combines ballistic missiles with cruise missiles, drones and decoys, forcing defenders to track numerous threats and ration rare interceptors, but Ukraine claims that it has too few batteries and interceptors to protect itself properly.
